trials.claim: One-time fee provides lifetime access to Koofr's service
trials.claimQuote: With a one-time fee, you get lifetime access to Koofr's service.
trials.reasoning: A buyer review confirms purchasing 1 TB for life at a one-time price; the prosecution exhibits describe ordinary subscription renewal terms and do not show lifetime-deal buyers being charged again or downgraded.

exhibits.quote: Payment of the subscription fee is upfront for the selected period and must be by credit card charge, PayPal® charge
exhibits.argument: Quote shows Koofr sells time-limited subscriptions requiring upfront payment per period, contradicting a one-time lifetime fee.

exhibits.quote: In case of non-renewal of subscription, your account is automatically switched to Free account, which means that quota
exhibits.argument: Quote proves access is not lifetime; failure to renew downgrades account and reduces quota, voiding lifetime claim.

exhibits.quote: and the price for 1 TB for life is excellent.
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms they purchased a 1 TB for life plan, supporting the one-time fee lifetime access claim.

trials.claim: Lifetime access is defined per Koofr terms of service and inactivity policy
trials.claimQuote: Lifetime access is defined in accordance with Koofr terms of service and inactivity policy.
trials.reasoning: Koofr's terms expressly define an inactivity policy requiring removal of long-inactive accounts, supporting that lifetime access is defined by those terms.

exhibits.quote: Due to EU privacy regulations, we are obligated to remove accounts that are not in active use for a long period of time.
exhibits.argument: Quote shows lifetime access is limited by an inactivity deletion policy, not indefinite access.

exhibits.quote: We may amend our Legal Terms at any time without specific notice to you.
exhibits.argument: Quote undermines defined lifetime terms because Koofr can unilaterally change terms without notice.

exhibits.quote: Due to EU privacy regulations, we are obligated to remove accounts that are not in active use for a long period of time.
exhibits.argument: Terms define an inactivity policy that limits lifetime access, supporting that lifetime is defined by the terms.

trials.claim: Offers 1TB of safe cloud storage to secure files

trials.reasoning: Vendor pricing lists a 1 TB XXL cloud storage plan; the yearly-subscription and over-quota exhibits concern ordinary accounts and do not contradict the 1TB offering.

exhibits.quote: Currently only yearly subscriptions are possible.
exhibits.argument: Quote contradicts 1TB lifetime offer by showing Koofr only sells yearly subscriptions.

exhibits.quote: If your account remains over quota for longer period of time, we may instruct you to remove some of your data or the data will
exhibits.argument: Quote undermines safe secure storage claim because data can be automatically removed when over quota after downgrade.
Vendor pricing lists a 1 TB plan, confirming Koofr offers 1TB of cloud storage.

trials.claim: 1TB lifetime plan provides ample space to store all important files
trials.claimQuote: With Koofr's 1TB lifetime plan, you have ample space to store all your important files.
trials.reasoning: No defense exhibit confirms the 1TB lifetime plan, and the prosecution exhibits only describe ordinary yearly subscriptions and non-renewal, which do not address deal buyers.

exhibits.quote: Currently only yearly subscriptions are possible.
exhibits.argument: Quote shows 1TB is sold as a yearly subscription, not a lifetime plan with ample permanent space.

exhibits.quote: In case of non-renewal of subscription, your account is automatically switched to Free account, which means that quota
exhibits.argument: Quote proves 1TB space is not permanent; non-renewal cuts quota to 10GB, contradicting ample lifetime space.

trials.claim: Access files anywhere, anytime on smartphone, personal computer, or WebDav
trials.claimQuote: Whether you're on your smartphone, personal computer, or using WebDav, you can access your files anywhere, anytime.
trials.reasoning: The vendor states access via any browser, desktop apps for Windows, Mac and Linux, and iOS, Android and Huawei mobile apps; the generic 'as is' disclaimer does not materially contradict that access.

exhibits.quote: YOU UNDERSTAND AND AGREE THAT THE SERVICES ARE PROVIDED TO YOU ON AN “AS IS” AND “AS AVAILABLE” BASIS.
exhibits.argument: Quote contradicts anywhere anytime guarantee by disclaiming availability and uptime warranties.

exhibits.quote: We may amend our Legal Terms at any time without specific notice to you.
exhibits.argument: Quote undermines guaranteed access because terms allowing unilateral changes can restrict availability.

exhibits.quote: Access your cloud storage from any browser, use our desktop app on your Windows, Mac or Linux computer, and sync on the go with our iOS, Android, and Huawei apps.
exhibits.argument: Vendor states files can be accessed via browser, desktop computer and mobile apps, supporting anywhere anytime access claim.

trials.claimQuote: Plus, you can easily connect to existing cloud accounts like Dropbox, Google Drive, Amazon, and OneDrive, making it a centralized computing solution.
trials.reasoning: The vendor lists external connections only for Dropbox, OneDrive and Google Drive, omitting Amazon despite the claim promising all four providers.
